parsed.why: Interior ministry can deport perceived-queer travellers without charge; police entrapment via apps targets trans women; forced anal exams and custody abuse documented; morality/sex-work prosecutions carry prison. Last dated arrest 2017; the state is the perpetrator.

Sodomy law enforced sporadically; police are a documented source of violence against trans and gay people with little accountability. Mob violence goes unpunished. A tolerant village and traditional third-gender recognition offset this only partly.

Documented protections in force: nationwide anti-discrimination in education and employment, a constitutional equality interpretation, and a conversion-therapy ban. No documented border or custody targeting of visitors. Facilities friction is minor, and the surgery-based ID rule is resident-facing.

Criminal statute carries up to two years. Police and prosecutors refuse to act on crimes against LGBTQ people, and official hostility is explicit. Social hostility is documented, and there is no anti-discrimination law. Enforcement evidence is thin, but the structure is severe.

Comprehensive protections cover gender identity, with recognition not requiring medical treatment and local disclosure removed. Pride attacks and under-recorded violence, plus weak enforcement and uneven official response, pull the score below the top tier.
